sources.note: ACIAR's own John Allwright Fellowship programme page (programme description, benefits, eligibility criteria, application status). Direct fetch returned HTTP 403 (bot protection), so the page content was read as verbatim live-crawl excerpts of this URL, cross-checked across two independent searches.
Official JAF factsheet PDF (linked from the ACIAR page, dated 12 December 2025). States the annual application window and the eligible degree types.
DFAT Online Australia Scholarships Information System (OASIS) news page, confirming the application scheme and that the 2027 intake has closed.

awarding_body.detail: The page is ACIAR's own domain (aciar.gov.au) and presents the John Allwright Fellowship run by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research, administered through the Australia Awards system. This matches the record's awarding body exactly.
awarding_body.quote: The John Allwright Fellowship (JAF) is a competitive, merit-based program available to scientists or economists from partner countries currently or recently involved in ACIAR research projects. It offers the opportunity to obtain formal postgraduate qualifications at an Australian tertiary institution.

deadline.detail: The page's current status banner reads 'Applications closed' and 'Applications for the 2027 intake are now closed.' The official factsheet states the recurring annual window: 'Applications open 1 February - 30 April'. The record's deadline (30 April 2026) matches the 2027 intake's close date, but that cycle has already closed, so as of 12 October 2026 there is no currently-open cycle and no open deadline can be confirmed. The next intake is expected to open 1 February 2027.
deadline.quote: Applications for the 2027 intake are now closed.

eligibility.detail: Each distinct eligibility claim in the record is confirmed on the official page: scientists or economists from partner countries, currently or recently involved in ACIAR research projects, seeking postgraduate qualifications at an Australian tertiary institution. The page adds further requirements not in the record (no Australian citizenship/PR, endorsement by employer and ACIAR project leaders, permanent or long-term employment, bachelor-equivalent qualifications, recent English test) which do not contradict the record.
eligibility.quote: You are a scientist or economist who is actively involved in an ACIAR research project or small research activity within the last 24 months.

funding.detail: The record's 'Fully Funded' claim is supported by the official benefits list: full tuition fees, return economy air travel, establishment allowance, a fortnightly Contribution to Living Expenses stipend, Introductory Academic Program, Overseas Student Health Cover, possible pre-course English fees, supplementary academic support and fieldwork airfares. This is a genuinely fully funded award, not tuition-only.
funding.quote: The following benefits generally apply: * Full tuition fees * Return air travel - payment of a single return, economy class airfare to and from Australia, via the most direct route * Establishment allowance - a once only payment as a contribution towards accommodation expenses, textbooks, study materials * Contribution to Living Expenses (CLE) - a fortnightly contribution to basic living expenses paid at a rate determined by the department.

degree_levels.detail: The programme offers research postgraduate degrees: the official factsheet states a Master by Research or PhD at an Australian tertiary institution, matching the record's 'Master's, PhD'. The factsheet explicitly excludes coursework masters: 'Masters by coursework is not eligible under this scholarship.'
degree_levels.quote: an opportunity to obtain formal postgraduate qualifications, such as a Master by Research or PhD degree at an Australian tertiary institution

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Annual application window (official factsheet): 'Applications open 1 February - 30 April'. As of 12 October 2026 the ACIAR page shows 'Applications closed' - applications for the 2027 intake closed on 30 April 2026 and the next intake (expected 2028) is due to open around 1 February 2027.
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: All substantive claims (awarding body, eligibility, funding, degree levels) confirmed against aciar.gov.au on 12 October 2026. The only blocker for an 'active' verdict is that the annual application window (1 February - 30 April) is closed: the 2027 intake closed 30 April 2026, confirmed by the ACIAR page banner and the DFAT OASIS news page. Re-check when the next intake opens, historically 1 February each year (expect the 2028 intake, closing 30 April 2027). Note for future automated re-checks: aciar.gov.au returns HTTP 403 to scripted fetchers; read via a normal browser or live search crawl. Degree levels: Master by Research or PhD only - Masters by coursework is explicitly not eligible.

notes_for_reviewer: The record is substantively accurate on every content claim, but the application round is not open on 12 October 2026 (the 2027 intake closed 30 April 2026), so under the campaign rule that the deadline must belong to a currently-open cycle it cannot be promoted to 'active' now. Recommend re-verifying in February 2027 when the next intake opens; if the factsheet window and benefits are unchanged it can then be marked active. If the catalogue must display a deadline today, the honest wording is the recurring 'applications open 1 February - 30 April each year' with the last close date of 30 April 2026.
